newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca drop on asthma drug reports.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca drop on asthma drug reports.

text.p: UK pharmaceuticals giant Zeneca Group Plc saw its shares shed 45-1/2 pence to 2017-1/2 on unconfirmed market reports on Thursday that its recently-launched asthma drug Accolate has caused serious side effects in a small number of cases.
Zeneca was not available for immediate comment.
Robin Gilbert, drugs analyst at Panmure Gordon, said "The fall is due to a side-effect story relating to Accolate. It involves a very small number of cases."
He added that Zeneca was not accepting a link but planned to examine the cases involved.
Accolate is the first in a new generation of asthma drugs and was recently launched by Zeneca in the U.S., where sales are eventually seen reaching hundreds of millions of dollars, say analysts.

Gilbert played down the significance of the reports, carried by a news agency, saying the side effects only impacted on a small number of people and was confident that sales targets would eventually be reached.
